purpose: Fenofibrate is used to lower high triglycerides (a type of fat) in your blood and to help raise your good cholesterol (HDL). It is also used to lower certain other unhealthy fats in your blood. Keeping these levels in a healthy range helps protect your heart and blood vessels.
how_it_works: Fenofibrate works by activating a protein in your body that controls how fats are made and broken down. This causes your liver to produce fewer triglycerides and helps your body clear them from your blood more quickly. Think of it like turning down the factory that makes unhealthy fats and speeding up the cleanup crew.
common_side_effects: Stomach upset, nausea, or belly pain are fairly common, especially when you first start the medicine. You may also notice muscle aches, headache, back pain, or a runny nose. Some people get abnormal liver blood test results, so your doctor may check your blood periodically.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have severe muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine, as this could signal a rare but serious muscle problem called rhabdomyolysis. Fenofibrate can affect your liver, so avoid heavy alcohol use and let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney disease. It can also interact with blood thinners like warfarin, so dosing of those medicines may need adjustment. Do not take if you are pregnant or breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one tablet or capsule taken once daily, typically with a meal to help your body absorb it better and reduce stomach upset. Doses commonly range from 40 mg to 160 mg per day depending on the specific brand and your individual needs. Always follow your doctor's instructions and do not stop taking it without checking with your healthcare provider first.
